subject: Weird arrangement of NA's and occurrences with the detectionHistory function

messages.author: ce5532ce531740ac
messages.subject: Weird arrangement of NA's and occurrences with the detectionHistory function
parts:
Dear Dr. Jorgen, I am coming to you for help with a problem I have experiencing in creating my detection-non-detection matrices using the detectionHistory function in camtrapR. I have searched in previous group discussions but did not find a similar problem.

I performed a CT sampling that started on December 16, 2016 and ended on March 20, 2017. (Below is attached the camera operation matrix)

I accumulated a total of 95 continuous days of sampling and obtained them by means of 30 spatially replicated camera traps at another site, accumulating a total of 61 cameras. Since my sampling was spatially replicated, I would expect my detection histories to have an alternate structure of NA blocks where the sites from the first spatial replicate were not active during the sampling of the second one and vice versa.

At the time of creating the operation matrix, I do not experience any inconvenience and when previewing it I can see that my NA's are distributed accordingly to the start and end dates of each sampling site.

To create the matrix of independent records every 24h I did not experience any problem either. However, when I run the function with the data I obtained independently for each 24h, it occurs that when the matrix comes out, half of its fields appear with 0's and the other half with NA's, which doesn't match with the NA's blocks nor with the detection history that I was spectating.

I attach my version of the script as well as the previously mentioned arrays.

# Load data

data_indp24h<- read.csv("datadep_24h.csv", header = T) # 24h records

actividad_cam <- read.csv("camera_act_UC.csv", header = T) # operation matrix

View(actividad_cam)

#Operation matrix

actividad_cam_2 <- cameraOperation(CTtable = actividad_cam, 
stationCol = "Station", 
setupCol = "start_date", 
retrievalCol = "end_date",
hasProblems = F,
dateFormat = "%d/%m/%Y")

#Create detection history

hist_captura_perspicax <- detectionHistory(recordTable = data_indp24h,                                camOp = actividad_cam_2,                                       
            stationCol = "Station",
            speciesCol = "Species", 
            recordDateTimeCol = "DateTimeOriginal", 
            recordDateTimeFormat = "%d/%m/%Y", 
            species = "Penelope_perspicax", 
            occasionLength = 5,
            day1 = "station",
           includeEffort = T,
           scaleEffort = TRUE,
           timeZone = "America/Mexico_City")

#detection history

detecciones <- hist_captura_perspicax [[1]]

duracion <- hist_captura_perspicax [[2]]

Can you give me a hand with the origin of my problem and explain me how I can solve it?

Cheers! 

Juan.

messages.subject: Re: Weird arrangement of NA's and occurrences with the detectionHistory function
parts:
Hi Juan,

I had a look at your data and here's what I found.

There were typos in

-> They should both the upper case.

Then I get  camera operation matrix, which looks like you did sampling in two time periods (see attachment, created with camopPlot). That corresponds to the setup/ retrieval dates in your table.


I can't run detectionHistory because of the following error: 

"Not all values of stationCol in recordTable are matched by rownames of camOp"

And indeed, the record table has station names like "C1", the camera table has "CT-UC-01-01" etc. So detectionHistory can't match the stations in the record table with the stations in the camera operation matrix and gives an error. That would need to be fixed so the stations match.

Normally you should not even be able to run your script, but receive error messages instead.

In detectionHistory, you should not see these two blocks as in the plot below because you set    day1 = "station". So the detection history at station should begin on the first occasion (first column).  I'm sorry I can't be more specific because I can't run detectionHistory with the data you shared.

Best regards,

Jürgen

The issue has been resolved! 

My mistake was set day1 = "station" instead of "survey". 

Thanks Dr Jorgen!
